Banana Circles are a thing. Here is approximately how I have seen them done.

  1. Pick an area that is at least 6 feet square. i.e. 6 ft by 6 ft.
  2. Dig a deep hole in the center of this square. Fill the hole with a lot of organic matter - leaves, twigs, food scraps, whatever.
  3. Around the edge of this hole, plant the banana saplings in a circle. If you look at the root of the sapling, you will see which side it was attached to the mother plant's root. The fruit will grow on the opposite side of where the mother plant was. Use this to position your plant so that the fruit grows to the outside of the circle.
  4. Over the growing season, keep dumping food-scraps and organic matter into that hole in the middle. That becomes the compost pit that feeds the banana plants. The leaves of the plants will grow to cast shade on this hole, which minimizes evaporation and helps conserve water near the roots.
  5. You can interplant the banana plants with smaller plants like beans or eggplant or whatever, to make more dense use of this system.

That's basically all I know about it. Hope this helps.
